title: Karna bows to his father
hook: crowned a king in the arena, Karna bows to the old charioteer who raised him, and pays for it with an insult
carry: pitru devo bhava: honor the one who raised you
tomorrow: why send the Pandavas on holiday?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Karna matched Arjuna, and Kunti knew her son and kept silent. The wise see one self in everyone.

Two fighters are ready to face each other. Then Kripa, one of the teachers, steps between them with a question that sounds polite. Arjuna is a prince, son of Pandu and Kunti. Tell us your mother and father, your royal line. A prince fights only an equal. And Karna, who has just matched every feat in the arena, has no answer to give. The text says he lowers his face.
screen: `KRIPA ASKS FOR HIS LINEAGE.` → `A PRINCE FIGHTS ONLY AN EQUAL.` → `KARNA LOWERS HIS FACE.`

segments.voice: Duryodhana jumps in. If Arjuna will only fight a king, then let Karna be a king. And there in the arena he has Karna crowned king of Anga. Karna, overwhelmed, asks what he can give in return. Duryodhana asks only for his friendship, and Karna gives it. Then, through the crowd, comes an old man, trembling, his cloth slipping. It's Adhiratha, the charioteer who pulled a basket from the river. And Karna, the new king, his hair still wet from the crowning, bows his head to him and greets him as his father. Adhiratha holds him and weeps. It's the moment Bhima has been waiting for. You're a charioteer's son, he says, so pick up a whip; you're not fit to fight Arjuna, or to rule Anga. Duryodhana defends his friend: the origins of heroes, like the sources of rivers, are hard to know. Then the sun sets, and the day ends with nothing settled. Now go back to that bow. Hindus have an old teaching for it. In the Taittiriya Upanishad, a teacher sends his students home with these words: let your mother be a god to you, let your father be a god to you, your teacher, and your guest. Matru devo bhava, pitru devo bhava. It's why Hindu children still bend to touch the feet of parents and elders, at festivals, before exams, before a big day, and receive a hand on the head and a blessing. Karna could have pretended not to know the old man. Everyone was watching. He bowed instead, and paid for it with an insult.
screen: `DURYODHANA CROWNS HIM KING OF ANGA.` · `KARNA BOWS TO ADHIRATHA.` · `BHIMA: PICK UP A WHIP.` · `PITRU DEVO BHAVA.` · then, large: `HONOR THE ONE WHO RAISED YOU.`

segments.voice: If a parent, grandparent or elder is near today, try the old greeting: bend and touch their feet, or bow with joined hands, and let them bless you. If no one's near, picture the one who raised you, the way Karna saw Adhiratha coming through the crowd, and bow to them in your mind. If you don't pray, a call or a message of thanks is the same bow.
Karna's abandonment. Asked his lineage, he lowers his face; crowned king, he bows to the charioteer who raised him; and the secret of his birth goes on following him.
Your line: pitru devo bhava, honor the one who raised you. A new king bowed to a charioteer. Tomorrow: why send the Pandavas on holiday?
